title: Activation Energy and Catalysts
short: A catalyst opens a path with a lower energy barrier and is not used up.
trouble: Students think a catalyst gets used up, or that it changes how much energy the reaction releases.

blocks.html: Collision Theory and Reaction Rate said that a collision must reach the activation energy to react. On an energy diagram, that requirement is a hill between the reactants and the products, and a catalyst is a way around it.

The activation energy $E_a$ is the climb from the reactants to the top of the energy hill. A catalyst provides a different pathway with a lower hill, so more collisions succeed and the reaction speeds up. The catalyst is not used up, and it does not change $\Delta H$: the reactants and products sit at the same energies as before.

A catalyst takes part in the reaction and is given back at the end. A metal surface, for example, holds reactant molecules so that their old bonds weaken as new ones start to form, and an enzyme's active site does the same for the molecules in a cell. The route changes; the starting point and the end point do not. A lower hill also helps the reverse reaction, so a catalyst speeds up both directions equally.

blocks.cap: Turn the catalyst on and off. The hill drops, but the reactants, the products and $\Delta H$ stay exactly where they were.

blocks.cap: The same box with a catalyst switch: with a lower $E_a$, many more collisions succeed at the same temperature.

blocks.title: Reading an energy diagram
blocks.q: Reactants are at $100\ \text{kJ}$, the top of the hill at $180\ \text{kJ}$ and the products at $40\ \text{kJ}$. Find $E_a$ and $\Delta H$.

blocks.title: Adding a catalyst
blocks.q: A catalyst lowers the peak in the same reaction to $130\ \text{kJ}$. What are the new $E_a$ and $\Delta H$?

blocks.html: Thinking a catalyst gets used up, or that it changes how much energy the reaction releases. A catalyst comes out unchanged, which is why a car's catalytic converter keeps working for years and a little enzyme handles a lot of reaction. Check on the diagram: only the height of the hill changes.
